prompt: The table gives the one-way commute times of $40$ employees, grouped as in a histogram. What percent of the employees commute less than $20$ minutes?
hint: Each bar covers a range of times. Decide which bars lie completely below $20$ minutes before you count anyone.

hints.text: Each bar covers a range of times. Decide which bars lie completely below $20$ minutes before you count anyone.
The $0$ to $10$ bar holds $4$ employees and the $10$ to $20$ bar holds $10$. Add those counts, then divide the sum by the total of $40$.
$4 + 10 = 14$ and $\frac{14}{40} = 0.35$, so $35$ percent of the employees commute less than $20$ minutes.

explanation: A commute under $20$ minutes falls in either the $0$ to $10$ bar or the $10$ to $20$ bar, so those are the two bars to use.
Adding their counts gives $4 + 10 = 14$ employees with a commute below $20$ minutes.
The whole group is $40$ employees, so the fraction is $\frac{14}{40} = 0.35$.
As a percent, $35$ percent of the employees commute less than $20$ minutes.

alternativeExplanations.title: Count the other side instead
steps: Employees at $20$ minutes or more: $16 + 10 = 26$, which is $\frac{26}{40} = 65$ percent.
Everyone is either under 20 or at least 20, so the rest is $100 - 65 = 35$ percent.
